summary: The Linux template uses free-spacing regex to capture index, name, flags, MTU and state, derives booleans like loopback and up from the flags, and a second entry captures inet address and mask; shared carries the name.
questions: How do I write a readable regex in a native template?
How do I turn interface flags into booleans with cli_parse?

answer_card.title: Linux ip addr template
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- example: '1: lo: <LOOPBACK,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 65536 ... state UNKNOWN ...'
  getval: |
    (?x)
    \d+:\s
    (?P<name>\S+):\s
    <(?P<properties>\S+)>
    \smtu\s(?P<mtu>\d+)
    .*
    state\s(?P<state>\S+)
  result:
    "{{ name }}":
      loopback: "{{ 'LOOPBACK' in properties.split(',') }}"
      up: "{{ 'UP' in properties.split(',') }}"
      state: "{{ state|lower() }}"
      mtu: "{{ mtu }}"
  shared: True
```
`(?x)` free-spacing mode allows inline comments; `shared` makes `name` available to the next entry (which captures `inet` and mask bits).
